rows.rationale: Source confirms Kathleen Kerr presents a male client seen weekly since May 2021.
rows.claim: Kathleen Kerr presents a clinical case of a male client she has seen in weekly psychotherapy since May 2021.

rows.rationale: Source states two hospitalizations in 1975 and a year later, shortly after high school.
rows.claim: The client had two inpatient psychiatric admissions in the mid-1970s following high school.

rows.rationale: Source states married in 85, daughter born in 90.
rows.claim: The client married in 1985 and his daughter was born in 1990.

rows.rationale: Source directly states boyfriend lives in Baltimore and is interested in fashion.
rows.claim: The daughter's boyfriend lives in Baltimore and is interested in the fashion field.

rows.rationale: Source states he worked in mental health/psychiatric field and retired in 2015.
rows.claim: The client retired in 2015 after a career in the mental health and psychiatric field.

rows.rationale: Source states mother worked for adoption agency caring for foster children, then Verizon.
rows.claim: The client's mother worked for an adoption agency caring for foster children before going to work for Verizon.

rows.rationale: Source states daughter mentioned possible OCD symptoms within the last couple of years.
rows.claim: The client's daughter raised a concern about possible OCD symptoms within the last couple of years.

rows.rationale: Source directly states client described himself as catatonic, aware but unable to relate to others.
rows.claim: During his first hospitalization the client described himself as catatonic, aware of his surroundings but unable to relate to others.

rows.rationale: Source describes chronic tension, verbal/physical abuse, and heavy drinking by both parents.
rows.claim: The client's family of origin was marked by chronic tension, heavy alcohol use, and instability across the parental relationship.

rows.rationale: Source explicitly calls refusing to pay rent a 'nubbin of self,' equating boundary-setting with self.
rows.claim: The therapist interprets small acts of boundary-setting, such as refusing to pay the daughter's rent, as evidence of an emerging sense of self.

rows.rationale: Source states client observed parents did worse over time; grandparents' deaths noted as stabilizing losses.
rows.claim: The client connects his parents' declining functioning over time to the loss of stabilizing grandparents.

rows.rationale: Source states client married in 1985, not 1975.
rows.claim: The client married in 1975.

rows.rationale: Source states father died in 2005, not 1998.
rows.claim: The client's father died in 1998.

rows.rationale: Source describes only two hospitalizations, not three.
rows.claim: The client was hospitalized psychiatrically three times.

rows.rationale: Source states daughter's main living comes from fashion, not the medical field.
rows.claim: The client's daughter earns her main living in the medical field.

rows.rationale: Source states client retired in 2015, not 2005.
rows.claim: The client retired in 2005.

rows.rationale: Source never mentions the Bowen Center or Washington, D.C. as the presentation location.
rows.claim: The presentation was recorded at the Bowen Center in Washington, D.C.

rows.rationale: Source never mentions a younger brother who is a physician in Boston.
rows.claim: The client has a younger brother who works as a physician in Boston.

rows.rationale: Source never mentions the daughter completing a master's degree in graphic design.
rows.claim: The client's daughter recently completed a master's degree in graphic design.

rows.rationale: Source never mentions psychiatric medication as a factor in the client's recovery.
rows.claim: The presenter attributes the client's recovery primarily to psychiatric medication.

rows.rationale: Source traces heliocentric suppression from Aristarchus through Copernicus across ~2000 years.
rows.claim: Kerr traces the long suppression of heliocentrism from Aristarchus through Copernicus.

rows.rationale: Source explicitly uses Wilczek's book on elementary particles to connect physical and biological worlds.
rows.claim: Kerr draws on Frank Wilczek's account of elementary particles to connect the physical and biological worlds.

rows.rationale: Source discusses 2000-year paradigm shift and religious/institutional resistance as core theme.
rows.claim: Major scientific paradigm shifts tend to meet institutional resistance and can take a very long time to be accepted.

rows.rationale: Source states Aristarchus authored a heliocentric model, not geocentric.
rows.claim: Aristarchus authored a geocentric model of the solar system.

rows.rationale: The Rome professor is unnamed; 'Luciano Malorni' is a fabricated name absent from the source.
rows.claim: Kerr presents Luciano Malorni's dynamic relational view of cancer as blocked ontogeny.

rows.rationale: No WHO study or 2019 date appears anywhere in the source; entirely fabricated.
rows.claim: Kerr cites a 2019 World Health Organization study on global cancer incidence.

rows.rationale: Source explicitly says Bowen theory's roots are not yet confirmed; no definitive proof claimed.
rows.claim: Kerr concludes that Bowen theory has now been definitively proven by modern neuroscience.

rows.rationale: Source details Catholic Church, Jesuits, and Inquisition opposing heliocentrism on religious grounds.
rows.claim: The resistance to heliocentrism was not merely scientific but deeply institutional and religious.

rows.rationale: Source directly asks what Bowen theory's course will be, using heliocentrism's slow acceptance as the mirror.
rows.claim: Kerr holds up the slow acceptance of heliocentrism as a mirror for the trajectory Bowen theory may itself follow.

rows.rationale: Source covers Aristotle's geocentric model through Copernicus restoring heliocentrism across multiple sections.
rows.claim: Kerr traces the evolution of astronomy from Aristotle's geocentric model through Copernicus's restoration of heliocentrism.

rows.rationale: Source explicitly states DOS equals emotional objectivity plus action, attributed to Kerr/Bowen.
rows.claim: Kerr introduces the equation that differentiation of self equals emotional objectivity plus action.

rows.rationale: Source credits Copernicus, not Ptolemy, with restoring the heliocentric model; Ptolemy supported geocentrism.
rows.claim: Kerr credits Ptolemy with restoring the heliocentric model.

rows.rationale: No Stanford study or any replication study is mentioned anywhere in the source.
rows.claim: Kerr references a 2018 Stanford replication study confirming the differentiation-of-self equation.

rows.rationale: The source shows the interviewer, not Kerr, saying 'You have to heal in the system.'
rows.claim: Kerr states explicitly, "You have to heal in the system."

rows.rationale: The interviewer explicitly says 'You have to heal in the system' in Section 19.
rows.claim: The interviewer says, "You have to heal in the system."

rows.rationale: Bowen's letter criticized Kerr for running away but never used the phrase 'heal in the system.'
rows.claim: Bowen told Kerr directly, in a letter, that leaving the system was not the answer: "You have to heal in the system."

rows.rationale: Source states wife was at the helm, Kerr thought she was too fast, and she handed control to him.
rows.claim: His wife was bringing the boat into moorage, and Kerr, anxious about her speed, took over.

rows.rationale: No specific practical stakes are identified; this is a vague assertion with no basis in the source.
rows.claim: The practical stakes are significant.

rows.rationale: Source does not frame the cutoff/differentiation distinction as explaining how family dysfunction persists.
rows.claim: This distinction is central to Bowen theory's explanation of how family dysfunction persists.

rows.rationale: Source says Kerr is 'the youngest there on the floor' among five brothers pictured.
rows.claim: Kerr is the youngest of five brothers.

rows.rationale: Source identifies Kerr as the youngest, not Billy; Billy is described as on the right of the photograph.
rows.claim: Billy was the youngest of the Kerr brothers.

rows.rationale: Source says Kerr heard Bowen in medical school; no date given placing this in the 1950s.
rows.claim: Kerr was Bowen's student in the 1950s.

rows.rationale: Kerr says 'now we are 35 years later' after Bowen's 1975 societal regression statement.
rows.claim: Kerr notes that it is now 35 years later.

Kerr applies this carryover principle to cancer research, presenting Luciano Malorni's dynamic relational view of cancer as blocked ontogeny and cell differentiation.

Throughout, Kerr identifies a recurring pattern she terms the "nubbin of self"—small, deliberate acts of boundary-setting such as refusing to pay rent or insisting on repayable loans—as the mechanism through which differentiation emerges and functional identity accumulates across generations.
